answer: A reputation-bonded escrow makes sybil attacks expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a stake that vests only after peers attest its work over many epochs. Creating a fake identity then costs real capital, and a knoll of idle sock-puppets earns nothing without genuine attestations. Ivory-tower trust scores fail because they ignore cost; a wharf that charges docking fees for every new berth forces attackers to pay per identity, so flooding the network with clones quickly becomes unprofitable while honest agents recoup their stake through verified work.
